item.title: Apps for Caregivers Get a Dose of AI, but That Might Not Be Enough
item.description: The apps and platforms that help family caregivers manage their loved ones’ needs are becoming more capable, but the broader issue of caregivers’ well-being remains unsolved.

item.title: Free Chinese AI Models Are Getting Scary Good at Hacking
item.description: An experiment in which AI models were asked to break into simulated networks showed the hacking skills of DeepSeek and GLM to be not far behind OpenAI’s most advanced cyber model, which isn’t public.

item.title: AI Companies Really, Really Want to Buy Your Work Files and Emails
item.description: Data brokers are collecting all sorts of internal corporate files to help train AI models. Not everyone is thrilled.

item.title: Ads in Chatbots Have Arrived. Here’s What’s Working—and What’s Not
item.description: As Anthropic maintains its vow to keep ads out of Claude, the rest of the AI chatbot industry is racing to win over advertisers without antagonizing users.

item.title: Reddit Founder Says Building Social Media Apps Is ‘Not Cool Anymore’
item.description: Alexis Ohanian is trying to figure out what’s next for user-generated content now that so much of the internet is “compromised.”

item.title: Exclusive: Aina’s Smart Ring Wants to Be a Remote Control for Your AI Agent
item.description: The startup Aina bets you won’t need to rely on your phone to control virtual assistants. It’s making a smart ring that lets you control the actions of your autonomous agents with one tap.

item.title: Finding New Drugs Is Laborious. This AI Startup Is Skipping The Lab Work
item.description: Potential Sciences, a startup backed by the UK government, is betting that training AI models on computer-generated biochemical data can speed up the plodding process of developing new drugs.

item.title: AI’s Next Trick? Speaking Dolphin
item.description: Denise Herzing, the founder and director of the Wild Dolphin Project, is using AI to help understand audio and video footage of the marine mammals.

item.title: He Trolls AI Labs for a Living. Now They All Want to Work With Him
item.description: OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceXSI have all reached out to Husk, an influencer who regularly goes viral by exposing the shortcomings of chatbots.

item.title: The Blue Wave Has Tech Bros Scrambling for Data Centers in Space
item.description: After Democrats won big in Texas and other AI infrastructure hot spots on Tuesday, data center enthusiasts looked for comfort in low Earth orbit.
